findings.issue_text: **`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` and `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have swapped contents.** `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `category`, `diff_category`, `happy_category`, and `private_category` fabricators. Fabrication doesn't care about file names matching fabricator names, so tests still pass, but this is clearly an accidental file-content swap (likely from a bad `git mv`/copy during the change) and will confuse/mislead anyone touching category or embedding fabricators later, or cause someone to delete/rename one file assuming it's unused.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8`** — the `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice with no nil-guard. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., a malformed API request missing the `host` key, or `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` absent), this raises `NoMethodError` instead of a normal validation error, producing a 500 instead of a 422/JSON error.

**No uniqueness validation on `EmbeddableHost#host`.** Two rows can be created for the same host, each with a different category. `record_for_host` then non-deterministically picks `.first`, so which category wins for a given embed is undefined.

**`store.js.es6:189-212`** — the `_hydrateEmbedded` regex was broadened from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`, and this function runs for *any* model whose payload is serialized with `rest_serializer: true`, not just `embedding`/`embeddable-host`. This is a global behavior change to the shared REST adapter/store layer for the sake of one feature. Any other existing (or future) serializer that already uses `rest_serializer: true` and happens to have an attribute ending in `_id`/`_ids` that isn't meant to be auto-resolved/deleted will now silently have that key stripped and replaced.

**Controller specs are placeholder-only.** `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain a single trivial "is a subclass of AdminController" assertion — there is no test exercising `create`/`update`/`destroy` behavior (e.g., saving with a blank category falling back to `uncategorized_category_id`, save failure returning `render_json_error`, or the `show`/`update` actions actually serializing hosts). Given this is the core feature described in the PR title, this is materially under-tested compared to the `embed_controller_spec.rb` updates.

**No FK/DB integrity for `category_id`.** The migration creates `category_id` as a plain `integer, null: false` with no foreign key and no `validates :category, presence: true` on the model (aside from `belongs_to :category`, which under old Discourse/Rails Rack conventions here does not appear to enforce existence — no `validates_associated`/`inverse_of`/`required: true` shown). An admin could submit a non-existent `category_id` and have it persist silently, or a category could later be deleted leaving orphaned `embeddable_hosts` rows whose `category` resolves to `nil` (and `topic_embed.rb`'s `creator.create` would then be called with `category: nil`, defaulting to whatever `PostCreator` does with a nil category rather than a controlled fallback).

**`admin-embedding.js.es6`'s `saveChanges` action is dead code** — it's never referenced from `embedding.hbs` or any other template, only invokes `embedding.update({})` which is itself close to a no-op (the `EmbeddingController#update` action just re-fetches and re-serializes the same `OpenStruct`, it doesn't persist anything).

`config/locales/client.en.yml`: the `admin.embedding.edit` key is added but never referenced anywhere in the templates/components (the edit button uses only a `pencil` icon, no label). Dead locale string.

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` builds an `INSERT` via raw string interpolation of `h` (the pre-existing site-setting host value) into SQL. Since this only runs once against admin-controlled, pre-existing settings data it's low risk, but using `quote(h)`/parameterized execution would be safer and is cheap to do.

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` — `force: true` will silently drop-and-recreate the table if one already exists with that name; for a brand-new table this is unnecessary and could mask a name collision or a mis-ordered migration re-run.

`store.js.es6:200`: `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` — `Array#map` always returns an array (never falsy), so the `|| []` fallback is unreachable dead code; harmless but worth removing for clarity.

`embeddable-host.js.es6`'s `edit()` action sets `categoryId` from `host.category.id` but there's no reset of `categoryId` on `cancel()` for existing hosts — not currently observable as a bug since `edit()` always resets it before the next edit session, but it's a bit of implicit state to track.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` without any `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (or equivalent) and the migration creates no unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host`. The admin UI/controller (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create`) allows creating new records freely, so duplicates for the same normalized host are possible. Lookup uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no ordering, so when duplicates exist the chosen row (and thus category used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) is effectively undefined. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

Neither spec exercises any of the newly introduced controller behavior in the diff (e.g., `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy` parameter handling and fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, error rendering on save failure, or `Admin::EmbeddingController#show/update` serialization). This is directly verifiable from the added spec contents and represents materially inadequate test coverage for newly added core functionality.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as a required integer column (`null: false`) but does not add any database foreign key or model-level validation that the referenced `Category` actually exists. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, `host.category_id` is assigned directly from params and only falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` when blank—an arbitrary/non-existent integer would still persist. This can lead to orphaned rows (e.g., if a category is deleted) and nil/invalid category resolution in the app (e.g., the admin component’s `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')`, which will break if `host.category` is nil). So the integrity gap is real and introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`admin-embedding.js.es6`'s `saveChanges` action is dead code** — it's never referenced from `embedding.hbs` or any other template, only invokes `embedding.update({})` which is itself close to a no-op (the `EmbeddingController#update` action just re-fetches and re-serializes the same `OpenStruct`, it doesn't persist anything).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but the new `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` never invokes `saveChanges` (it only renders the hosts table and an `addHost` button). No other template/routes in the diff reference `saveChanges` either. Additionally, the new backend `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist anything; it just re-renders the same `@embedding` OpenStruct via `EmbeddingSerializer`, so even if called it would be effectively a no-op. This makes `saveChanges` dead/unnecessary code as introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/locales/client.en.yml`: the `admin.embedding.edit` key is added but never referenced anywhere in the templates/components (the edit button uses only a `pencil` icon, no label). Dead locale string.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin.embedding.edit: "edit"` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, and within the added/modified templates/components in this diff there is no reference to `admin.embedding.edit` (the edit control is `{{d-button icon="pencil" action="edit"}}` with no label/i18n key). However, this is not a functional bug or correctness issue—it's an unused translation string (a minor maintenance nit), and the diff alone cannot prove it’s not referenced elsewhere in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` builds an `INSERT` via raw string interpolation of `h` (the pre-existing site-setting host value) into SQL. Since this only runs once against admin-controlled, pre-existing settings data it's low risk, but using `quote(h)`/parameterized execution would be safer and is cheap to do.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads embeddable_hosts from the site_settings table, splits into lines, and for each line does:

execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

This is raw SQL string interpolation of h into a quoted SQL literal. If any stored host value contains a single-quote (or other SQL-special content), the migration can fail or potentially allow SQL injection in the migration context. Even if the data is admin-controlled, it’s still an actual correctness/security issue present in the diff and would be safer to use connection.quote(h) / parameterization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` — `force: true` will silently drop-and-recreate the table if one already exists with that name; for a brand-new table this is unnecessary and could mask a name collision or a mis-ordered migration re-run.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. In a migration intended to introduce a new table, this is unnecessary and can turn what would normally be a loud failure (table already exists due to a collision/misordered migrations) into silent data loss by dropping an existing `embeddable_hosts` table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `store.js.es6:200`: `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` — `Array#map` always returns an array (never falsy), so the `|| []` fallback is unreachable dead code; harmless but worth removing for clarity.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `_ids` hydration branch, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array object (truthy) when `obj[k]` is an Array, so `hydrated || []` will never use the fallback. However, this is purely a minor readability/dead-code nit; it does not create a functional bug, security issue, or correctness problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embeddable-host.js.es6`'s `edit()` action sets `categoryId` from `host.category.id` but there's no reset of `categoryId` on `cancel()` for existing hosts — not currently observable as a bug since `edit()` always resets it before the next edit session, but it's a bit of implicit state to track.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is only used in the editing UI (`{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}`) and when saving (`props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`). When cancelling an existing host, the component exits editing (`editToggled = false`) and the non-editing template displays `host.category` (not `categoryId`). On the next edit session, `edit()` always resets `categoryId` from `host.category.id`. So while `categoryId` isn’t explicitly reset on cancel, there’s no verifiable incorrect behavior introduced by this diff—it's at most implicit/leftover state, not an observable bug or defect.
